data.title: Royal Gold Files 8K - Director, Officer or Compensation Filing >RGLD
data.description:
Royal Gold Inc. (RGLD) filed a Form 8K - Director, Officer or Compensation Filing - with the U.S Securities and Exchange Commission on November 18, 2026.

On November 17, 2026, the Board of Directors (the "Board") of Royal Gold, Inc. (the "Company") approved an increase in the size of the Board from seven to eight members and appointed Harry Kenyon-Slaney to fill the resulting vacancy, effective immediately. Mr. Kenyon-Slaney will serve as a Class I director, with a term ending at the Company's 2027 annual meeting of stockholders. The Board has determined that Mr. Kenyon-Slaney is independent under the applicable Nasdaq listing standards.

There are no arrangements or understandings between Mr. Kenyon-Slaney and any other person pursuant to which he was selected as a director, and there are no related person transactions between Mr. Kenyon-Slaney and the Company that would be reportable under Item 404(a) of Regulation S-K. Mr. Kenyon-Slaney will receive compensation for his services on the Board in accordance with the Company's compensation program for non-employee directors as set forth under the heading "Director Compensation" in the Company's proxy statement for its 2026 annual meeting of stockholders. Mr. Kenyon-Slaney has not been appointed to any committees of the Board.

The full text of this SEC filing can be retrieved at: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/85535/000008553526000055/rgld-20261117.htm

data.title: Anthropic Is Eyeing Pricing Its IPO As High As $85 Per Share: Report
data.description:
Key points:
  • Pricing at the top of the $80 to $85 range would push Anthropic's total offering, which includes a $26 billion private placement, past $96 billion.
  • Major semiconductor firms, including Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices, have committed to purchasing shares in the private placement at the final IPO price. 
  • The company will list on the Nasdaq under the ticker ‘ANT’ on Thursday.

Claude developer Anthropic PBC is weighing an initial public offering price between $80 and $85 per share, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday.

The upper limit of that target range would generate as much as $70 billion from the base offering alone, according to people familiar with the internal IPO discussions quoted by Bloomberg. Combined with a separate $26 billion private placement, the total capital raised would exceed $96 billion, without expanding the number of shares available.

However, discussions are still underway and executives have not yet finalized the pricing. A representative for Anthropic did not immediately reply to Stocktwits’ request for comment.

Surpassing SpaceX

If finalized at the $85 mark, Anthropic's combined offering would surpass SpaceX's landmark debut, which raised $75 billion in its base offering and $86.2 billion after accounting for overallotment options.

Regulatory filings indicate that Anthropic previously marketed a base offering of 801.4 million shares, alongside 23.6 million shares offered by existing investors, at an initial target range of $70 to $78 per share.

Those filings also reveal that leading chipmakers, including Nvidia Corp.(NVDA) and Advanced Micro Devices Inc.(AMD), have agreed to participate in the $26 billion private placement at the eventual IPO price.

Additionally, assuming an approximate $1.5 trillion valuation, Anthropic (ANT) would command a valuation multiple of nearly 8.5 times projected revenue, aligning its pricing with mega-cap tech giants like Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) and Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL), according to New Street Research analyst Pierre Ferragu.

First Listed Frontier Lab

The debut represents a watershed moment for the technology sector, as Anthropic will become the first "frontier" AI laboratory to trade publicly, beating chief rival OpenAI, which is not expected to pursue a listing until at least 2027.

Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and Morgan Stanley are serving as the lead underwriters for the offering, supported by a syndicate of 20 additional financial institutions. Shares of Anthropic are scheduled to begin trading Thursday on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol ‘ANT’.

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits towards Anthropic was ‘extremely bullish’ ahead of its official pricing, with ‘extremely high’ message volumes.

data.title: StoneX Q4 EPS disappoints as net income falls 2% Y/Y
data.description:
StoneX Group stock slid 2.9% in Wednesday after-hours trading as the company's fiscal Q4 earnings failed to meet Wall Street expectations. While operating revenue grew from a year ago but fell from fiscal Q3, its expenses rose both from the prior quarter and a year ago.

Fiscal Q4 EPS of $0.66, trailing the average analyst estimate of $0.88, fell from $1.00 in Q3 and $0.70 in last year’s Q4. Net income of $84.2M fell from $127.9M in the previous quarter and $85.7M in the year-ago period.

Operating revenue of $1.46B for the quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026, edged down from $1.47B in the prior quarter and increased from $1.20B a year ago. Net operating revenue of $655.2M, which subtracts clearing expenses, broker commissions, and interest expenses, dipped from $719.7M in Q3 and climbed from $585.1M in Q4 2025.

Operating revenue by segment:

  • Commercial rose 57% Y/Y to $466.5M
  • Institutional increased 12% Y/Y to $859.7M
  • Self-directed/retail fell 7% to $75.7M.
  • Payments grew 19% Y/Y to $62.1M.

Net contribution of $440.4M fell from $475.7M in the previous quarter and grew from $401.9M in the year-ago period.

Total fixed compensation and other expenses increased to $320.0M from $314.2M in Q3 and $293.8M in last year’s Q4.

Adjusted EBITDA of $193.7M compared with $229.5M in the prior quarter and $170.9M a year ago.

Return on equity was 11.6%, down from $18.4% in the previous quarter and 15.2% a year ago.

Conference  call on Nov. 19 at 9:00 AM ET.

data.title: Has the stock market's correction hit bottom yet? Here's what these contrarian indicators say.
data.description:
By Mark Hulbert

Contrarian buy signals typically don't come until sentiment has dropped further than they have so far

We're not at the bottom yet, it appears.

The bottom of the stock market's correction is still ahead of us, according to contrarian analysis.

That surprises some traders, since the stock market's recent declines and extraordinary volatility has caused the mood on Wall Street to sour. Surely the veritable Wall of Worry that markets like to climb has been sufficiently rebuilt?

No, according to my auditing firm's monitoring of short-term market timers. Though it is true that they are less bullish than they were six weeks ago, they have not yet become bearish enough to satisfy contrarians' criteria for a buy signal.

Consider these timers' average recommended equity exposure level. The Hulbert Stock Newsletter Sentiment Index (HSNSI), which reflects this average among several dozen short-term market timers who focus on the broad stock market. As you can see from the accompanying chart, it has declined to just the upper edge of the excessively bearish zone that I have used in prior columns about market sentiment. That zone is defined as the range of readings in the bottom decile of the historical distribution.

Contrarian buy signals typically don't come until sentiment has dropped further into that zone and stays there for a number of trading sessions.

An even stronger indication that a buy signal would be premature comes from the Hulbert Nasdaq Newsletter Sentiment Index (HNNSI), which is a similar sentiment measure except that it includes a different group of timers - those who focus on the Nasdaq market in particular. (This second index is not in the accompanying chart.) This index has dropped even less than the HSNSI, which is surprising since the Nasdaq market has suffered significantly more in recent weeks than the broad market. While the S&P 500 SPX is 6.3% below its early October high, for example, the Nasdaq Composite COMP is 11.5% below.

Other sentiment measures are also suggesting that the decline has further to go. Consider the weekly sentiment survey that the American Association of Individual Investors conducts of its members. Those who say they are bullish, expressed as a percentage of those who are either bullish or bearish, just this week dipped to the upper end of what I have defined as the excessively bearish zone. The VIX VIX (Cboe's Volatility Index, aka the investor-fear index) is currently pointing away from being in its excessively bearish zone.

Surging demand for Anthropic's upcoming IPO provides yet more evidence of these pockets of bullishness. The company's IPO reportedly has been nearly seven times oversubscribed.

The bottom line: Sentiment is moving in the right direction to entice contrarians to declare that a tradable bottom is in. But it's not there yet.

Mark Hulbert is a regular contributor to MarketWatch. His Hulbert Ratings tracks investment newsletters that pay a flat fee to be audited. He can be reached at mark@hulbertratings.com

-Mark Hulbert
